representations.name: typed one-demand local switch gadget
representations.new_information: Stores the old base e, old K(e), a complete original-graph switch, new base e', and one named output f in K(e') minus K(e).
representations.repairs_loss: It distinguishes an external missing edge from a graph-proved legal arc to that edge.
representations.first_test: On the n=15 one-vertex expansion test all four replacements b-x_i by w-x_i; reject any switch producing a non-rainbow C7.
representations.public_effect: One compatible switch per locked deficit could increase actual carrier rank.

representations.name: multi-demand switch compatibility complex
representations.new_information: Records which individually legal switches may coexist, including shared recoloured edges, C7 witnesses, outputs and owners.
representations.repairs_loss: Individual switch counts no longer imply simultaneous cut expansion.
representations.first_test: Enumerate every subset of the four natural n=15 switches and compare catalogue size with distinct external outputs.
representations.public_effect: A compatible switch packing saturating each deficient cut would be an actual absorber theorem.

representations.name: output-projected DRC reservoir
representations.new_information: DRC is performed on distinct external missing B-edge outputs after projection, with every output fibre size retained.
representations.repairs_loss: Large path or C7-witness common neighbourhoods cannot masquerade as many carriers.
representations.first_test: The n=15 expansion has 736 length-four/five path witnesses but one external output; any pre-projection DRC bound must fail this test.
representations.public_effect: A post-projection common reservoir with small fibres could supply many actual outputs.

representations.name: cut-conditioned absorber reservoir
representations.new_information: For every deficient demand cut T it retains the number of distinct outside outputs adjacent to many members of T and not occupied outside T.
representations.repairs_loss: Global reservoir abundance cannot hide one locked cut with no expansion.
representations.first_test: Use the four-demand locked cut and the n=15 single-output expansion; reject a reservoir theorem whose cut image has size one.
representations.public_effect: Uniform projected expansion could feed Hall after construction.

representations.name: absorber hypergraph with output and witness codegrees
representations.new_information: Each hyperedge contains a demand, external output, and every graph resource consumed; degrees and all pair codegrees are explicit.
representations.repairs_loss: Parallel certificates sharing an output or indispensable witness are recognized as high-codegree edges.
representations.first_test: Project the 736 n=15 path witnesses to wz; their output codegree equals catalogue size and matching rank is at most one.
representations.public_effect: A graph-derived low-codegree nibble plus cleanup could allocate a sparse residue.

representations.name: all-cut nibble deficiency potential
representations.new_information: Tracks maximum Hall deficiency over all cuts together with untouched actual outputs after each nibble round.
representations.repairs_loss: Expected certificate or matching count cannot hide a persistent correlated cut.
representations.first_test: Exact outcome enumeration on a many-certificate one-output hypergraph must retain deficiency three for four demands.
representations.public_effect: Contraction followed by deterministic compatible-switch cleanup could globalize the absorber.

representations.name: actual-output matroid parity system
representations.new_information: Ground elements are concrete missing B-edges paired with exclusive switch-owner resources; feasibility is replayed in the original graph.
representations.repairs_loss: A-side owners and certificate copies cannot be added to B-output rank on different grounds.
representations.first_test: Test augmentation on four switch candidates sharing wz and on the locked four-owner/two-output graph.
representations.public_effect: A valid parity augmentation axiom could turn local switches into nonreused outputs.

representations.name: vertex-capacitated C7 linkage network
representations.new_information: Paths begin at named demands, traverse complete legal switch gadgets, and end at distinct external outputs; every internal graph resource has capacity one.
representations.repairs_loss: Abstract connectivity is separated from disjoint graph-realizable linkage.
representations.first_test: The n=15 candidate paths all terminate at wz and every proposed first switch fails rainbow-C7 legality.
representations.public_effect: A min-cut theorem in a genuinely represented network could certify cut expansion.

representations.name: absorber-preserving stability core
representations.new_information: The typical/exceptional split records, for each demand cut, how many external outputs and switch witnesses lie in every part.
representations.repairs_loss: A small exceptional set cannot silently contain all rank-increasing outputs.
representations.first_test: Place w and the sole external output wz in the exceptional part of the n=15 expansion; typical path abundance must not count as output expansion.
representations.public_effect: A stability theorem preserving output rank could reduce the global proof to finitely many core switch types.

representations.name: locked-core plus exceptional-link decomposition
representations.new_information: Contracts each identical-base locked class to its exact deficiency and records every exceptional legal arc leaving the class.
representations.repairs_loss: The core's large internal catalogue is replaced by the correct rank deficit, so only external links can pay it.
representations.first_test: Contract the n=14 class and its one-vertex expansion; the four natural links must be deleted when their switch is non-rainbow.
representations.public_effect: A lower bound on distinct exceptional links per contracted deficiency would give the required carrier creation.
